plugins.name: Combo Counter
plugins.summary: Counts the hits and damage of every combo as it lands, and keeps each player's best combo of the match.
plugins.description:
A live combo counter: while a combo is running, `4 HITS 37%` in the attacker's colour under the
timer; when it ends, the total stays up for a moment (`5 hit combo, 52%, KILL`). Each player's
best combo of the match is kept in the bottom-right corner.

A combo lasts while the victim stays punished (hit, tumbling, grabbed, thrown, knocked down,
teching) or gets fewer than 45 frames to act between hits: the same rule Slippi's stats use, so
the numbers agree with the replays you are used to. Both the threshold and the minimum number of
hits to show are settings.

Read-only: it never changes the game.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

settings.label: Show combos from this many hits
Frames free before a combo ends
Keep each player's best combo on screen

plugins.name: DI Trainer
plugins.summary: Shows where a hit will send you while you are frozen in hitlag: with no DI, with the DI you are holding, and with the DI that survives best.
plugins.description:
DI Trainer shows where a hit is about to send you, while you are still frozen in hitlag and can do something about it.

- The **grey** line is the path with no DI.
- The **yellow** line is the path with the DI you are holding right now. It moves with your stick until hitlag ends.
- The **green** line is the DI that survives with the most room to spare. If nothing survives, it is the DI that dies last.
- A **red X** marks where a path crosses a blast zone while you are still launched: a KO.

A small stick gauge beside the fighter shows your stick (yellow dot) and the best DI (green dot), with a verdict underneath: "Survives", "Your DI saves you", "KO: DI green to live" or "KO whatever the DI", and how many frames of hitstun the hit gives.

Press **F10** to show or hide the paths. You can turn off the grey or green line, and choose whether the paths stay on screen while you fly.

Train with it by setting a CPU on the other side and a kill percent with Training Lab's percent lock, then slow the game with F7 so hitlag lasts long enough to watch the lines move as you DI.

The prediction repeats what the game does when hitlag ends: automatic smash DI moves you 3 units along the stick if it is pushed past 0.7, then DI turns the launch by up to 18 degrees, most when the stick points across the launch. The flight uses your fighter's own gravity and fall speed and the stage's real blast zones. Both steps were checked against launches logged frame by frame in the game. Hits during the flight, platforms, walls and ceilings are not taken into account; the main floor is for Battlefield, Final Destination, Dream Land, Fountain of Dreams, Pokemon Stadium and Yoshi's Story. The plugin only reads game memory; it changes nothing.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

settings.label: Keep the path on screen while flying

plugins.name: Frame Data
plugins.summary: Shows each fighter's action state, frame, hitlag and hitstun, and who is plus after every hit or shield.
plugins.description:
Frame data on screen while you play, the way the practice tools in modern fighting games show it.

**State panels.** One small panel per fighter (port 1, ports 1 and 2, or everyone): the character,
what they are doing ("Nair f7", "Guard", "DamageFlyN"), and chips for hitlag, hitstun and
"CAN ACT", the moment the fighter can move again. A thin bar along the bottom is their shield.

**Frame advantage.** Every time an attack connects, on a body or on a shield, the plugin counts
the frames until each side can act again and shows the difference under the attacker's panel:

- `Jab on shield -10`: the defender can act 10 frames before you, so they can punish.
- `Nair on shield -24 (landed 12f later)`: aerials are only as safe as they are low; this one hit
  12 frames before landing. Hit lower (or L-cancel) and the number climbs.
- `Usmash: true combo`: the second hit came before the defender could act.

Positive numbers mean you are plus (green), negative mean minus (red). Pausing the game stops the
clock. Turn on **Show state ids and positions** to see raw action state ids and coordinates, handy
when you are writing a plugin of your own.

Read-only: it never changes the game.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

settings.label: Frame advantage after hits and shields

changelog.notes: On PascalPatch 0.5 the state panels share the top corners with other plugins' panels instead of drawing over them.

Shield advantage was 3 to 6 frames too harsh: the defender counted as free as soon as shield hitlag ended. It now waits for shield stun to end (checked frame by frame: Dr. Mario's jab is -10 on shield, not -13).

plugins.name: Hitbox Viewer
plugins.summary: Draws every fighter's hitboxes and hurtboxes over the game, with invincibility and intangibility shown in colour.
plugins.description:
Hitbox Viewer draws what the game actually tests for collisions, on top of the match.

- **Red** capsules are hitboxes. Each is drawn from where it was last frame to where it is now, because the game checks that whole swept shape.
- **Purple** capsules are grab boxes.
- **Yellow** capsules are hurtboxes: the parts of a fighter that can be hit.
- **Green** hurtboxes are invincible: hits connect but do nothing, as in the first frames of a ledge grab.
- **Blue** hurtboxes are intangible: hits pass straight through, as in rolls, spot dodges and air dodges.

Press **F3** to show or hide the boxes. You can change the key, turn either kind off, or make them fainter in the plugin's settings.

It pairs well with Training Lab: pause with F5 and step with F6 to see exactly which frame a move comes out, or where a dodge stops being intangible.

The boxes are projected with the game's own camera, so they follow zooms and camera shakes. The plugin only reads game memory; it changes nothing.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

plugins.name: Info Display
plugins.summary: A lab-style panel of each fighter's numbers (state and frame, position, velocities, jumps, shield, intangibility, ledge timer), plus a flash the frame a fighter can act again.
plugins.description:
Info Display shows the numbers behind each fighter, the way a training lab does, and flashes a fighter the moment they can act again.

**The panel** (one per fighter: port 1, ports 1 and 2, or everyone; top corners or halfway down the sides). Pick the rows you want:

- **State and frame**: the action state and how many frames it has lasted. Green once the fighter can act: out of hitstun, past its landing lag, into a move's interruptible frames.
- **Position**, **own velocity** and **knockback velocity** (yellow while a hit is still carrying the fighter).
- **Ground speed**, and whether the fighter is grounded or airborne.
- **Jumps left** out of the character's total, and walljumps used.
- **Shield health**, out of 60.
- **Intangibility**: frames of intangibility or invincibility left (after a ledge grab or a respawn), or "(move)" when the current move makes the fighter intangible, such as a roll or a spot dodge.
- **Ledge regrab timer**: frames until the fighter can grab the ledge again.
- **Hitlag and hitstun** frames left.
- **Stick and trigger**: the stick as the game reads it (after the dead zone) and the analog L/R.

**The actionable flash.** A green ring appears on a fighter the frame they can act after being stuck: hitstun, landing lag, shield stun, a knockdown, or the end of their own move. Watch for it to learn how long your moves leave you open, or when to punish.

Press **Insert** to hide or show everything. The plugin only reads game memory; it changes nothing. It sits well with Frame Data (frame advantage after hits) and Training Lab (pause and frame advance).
plugins.author: PascalPatch

settings.label: Flash when a fighter can act again
Flash every fighter, not just those with a panel

changelog.notes: On PascalPatch 0.5 the panels share the top corners with other plugins' panels instead of drawing over them.

plugins.name: Input Display
plugins.summary: Shows a controller's sticks, buttons and triggers on screen, for practice and recordings.
plugins.description:
Draws a GameCube controller in a corner of the screen: the control stick and C-stick positions,
A, B, X, Y, Z and Start, the D-pad, and how far L and R are pressed. Handy for practice,
tutorials and recordings.

Pick the port, the corner, the size and the opacity in the F2 window; changes show at once.
It only reads the controller state the game already reads, and never changes the game.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

plugins.name: Match Stats
plugins.summary: Openings, kills, damage per opening, neutral wins, L-cancel rate and inputs per minute for every match, with a history file.
plugins.description:
The numbers behind every match, Slippi-style, with no Slippi involved.

When a match ends, a card shows each player's:

- **Kills** and **openings** (punishes started), **openings per kill** and **damage per
  opening**: how well you convert.
- **Neutral wins**: openings started while nobody was being punished.
- **Damage** dealt, **L-cancel** rate and **inputs per minute**.

Hold **F4** during a match to see the card live. Tap it on the results screen to dismiss it.

Each finished match (longer than ten seconds) is also added as one line of JSON to
`match-stats.jsonl` beside the plugin, so you can chart your progress over a session or a month.
Turn that off in the F2 window if you prefer.

Read-only: it never changes the game.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

settings.label: Show the stats when a match ends
Hold to see the stats during a match

plugins.name: Tech Trainer
plugins.summary: Instant feedback on L-cancels, short hops, wavedashes, techs, out-of-shield timing, powershields, ledgedashes, SDI and fastfalls.
plugins.description:
Instant, specific feedback on Melee's timing-heavy techniques, so every attempt teaches you
something:

- **L-cancels**: `Nair L-cancelled (3/7)`, or `L 5 frames early`, `L-cancel: 2 frames late`,
  `Missed L-cancel`.
- **Hops**: `Short hop` or `Full hop` off every jump.
- **Wavedashes**: `Wavedash: frame 1 (perfect), 17 deg`, or which airborne frame the air dodge
  came on; it also warns when the stick was not angled down.
- **Techs**: `Teched forward`, or `Missed tech: L/R 6 frames early`.
- **Out of shield**: `Out of shield: Jump on frame 1 (no delay)`, or how many frames you waited
  after shield stun ended.
- **Powershields**: `Powershield! (frame 3 of 8)`, or `Powershield: L/R 2 frames too early`.
- **Ledgedashes**: `Ledgedash: 7 frames intangible after the lag (jump f2, dodge f1)`, or how
  long the landing was open to hits.
- **SDI**: `SDI: 4 inputs in 9 frames of hitlag, moved 24`, or `No SDI` on a long hitlag.
- **Fastfalls** (off by default): `Fastfall: frame 1 after the peak`.

Each one can be turned off in the settings.

A tally on the left keeps your success rate for the match (L-cancel 14/17, 82%, powershields, ledgedashes);
press **F8** (or the key you choose) to reset it. Coach one port or every human player.

The windows it checks are the game's own: 7 frames for an L-cancel, 20 for a tech. If you run the
port with auto L-cancel turned on, every landing counts as cancelled.

Read-only: it never changes the game.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

changelog.notes: Five new coaches, after UnclePunch's Training Mode: out-of-shield timing (the first action after shield stun and on which frame), powershields (or how many frames early the L/R press was), ledgedashes (intangibility left once the landing lag ends), SDI (inputs during hitlag and the distance moved) and fastfall timing (frames after the jump's peak). On PascalPatch 0.5 the tally shares the corner with other plugins' panels.

plugins.name: Training Lab
plugins.summary: Pause, frame advance and slow motion on hotkeys, plus percent reset and lock, infinite shield and endless stocks.
plugins.description:
Practice tools for any match, on hotkeys (rebind them in the F2 window):

- **F5 pause / resume** and **F6 frame advance**: freeze the game and step through a
  combo or a move one frame at a time. Pair it with Frame Data to see every state change.
- **F7 slow motion**: half or quarter speed, for learning timings by feel.
- **F9 reset percent**, or **lock** a player at a set percent to drill a kill confirm or a
  combo at exactly the percent it works at.
- **Infinite shield**: shields never shrink or break, for practising out-of-shield options.
- **Endless stocks**: nobody runs out, so a practice match never ends.

Percent, shield and stock options apply to the player you pick: port 1, port 2 (the default, your
practice partner), everyone, or only CPU players. Hotkeys only work while the game window has
focus and the F2 window is closed.

Pause and slow motion hold the game inside the frame; the window, the F2 window and other
plugins keep running. This plugin writes game memory (percent, shield, stocks) only while those
options are on.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

settings.label: Percent, shield and stock options apply to

plugins.name: Unlock All
plugins.summary: Every character and stage is selectable from the first boot, without touching your memory card.
plugins.description:
Opens all 26 characters and every stage straight away. Characters are set in the game's own
unlock flags each frame; stages are opened only while the VS character and stage select screens
are showing and put back before the match, so the game never plays its "new challenger" or
unlock notices. Nothing is written to the memory card unless the game saves by itself.

Both halves can be switched off in the F2 window.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

changelog.notes: A fresh save no longer boots into a run of "You got a trophy" notices: characters, like stages, are unlocked only while a select screen is up.

plugins.name: Wavedash Trainer
plugins.summary: Breaks down every wavedash: when you pressed L/R, the stick angle, how long it was against your character's best, and one tip to fix it.
plugins.description:
Wavedash Trainer breaks down every wavedash you do and tells you the one thing to change.

After each wavedash, a line above your damage meter gives the verdict ("Wavedash: frame 1, 17 deg, 100% length", "Too early: L/R 2 frames before the jump", "Stick too flat: the air dodge went sideways") and a tip. The panel in the top right shows:

- A **frame strip**: your jumpsquat (grey, with a red mark where you pressed L/R too early), the frames you spent in the air before the air dodge (orange), the air dodge itself, and the 10 frames of landing lag (blue).
- A **stick gauge**: the red band is the part of the stick the game reads as flat, the green lines are the shallowest angle that still wavedashes, and the yellow line is where your stick was.
- The **angle** and the **length**: how far this wavedash slid next to the longest your character can do, in percent and in units.
- The **gap**: frames between the end of one wavedash's landing lag and the next jump, when you chain them.
- Your last 16 attempts as coloured squares, and a count of perfect and clean ones. Press **F12** to reset the count.

What counts as perfect comes from the game itself:

- L/R pressed during jumpsquat does nothing. The earliest air dodge is on the frame jumpsquat ends, which goes straight from jumpsquat to the landing. That is "frame 1". Each frame later loses speed and length.
- Stick heights up to 0.28 read as zero, so a stick that is too flat air dodges sideways and never lands. The shallowest angle that works is about 17 degrees below horizontal, and it gives the longest slide.
- Because the air dodge is the same for everyone, the best wavedash lands at the same speed for every character; how far it slides depends on your character's traction (Luigi slides far, Peach barely moves).

Coach one port, or every human player at once. Out-of-shield wavedashes are labelled as such; straight-down ones count as wavedashes in place. The plugin only reads game memory; it changes nothing.
plugins.author: PascalPatch

changelog.notes: The verdict and the tip now sit inside the breakdown panel (wrapped to fit), so they no longer land on Tech Trainer's lines; on PascalPatch 0.5 the panel shares its corner with other plugins' panels.
